profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (QTS Ashburn Lockridge / ASH2 campus)
profile.reading:
Per a Baxtel listing (QTS's own current locations page lists "Ashburn 1, Ashburn 2, Ashburn 3, and Ashburn Moran" without street addresses), the Lockridge/ASH2 campus sits at 44675 Quality Tech Lane, Ashburn, VA, a 28-acre infill site with two bookend buildings, ASH2 DC1 and ASH2 DC2; this registry carries three separate map entries sharing this Lockridge name clustered within roughly 100 meters, and since QTS's own naming does not publish separate street addresses per building, the one confirmed campus address is applied to all three rather than guessing which specific building each represents.

QTS Data Centers (shown on this row under its pre-2013-IPO name, "Quality Technology Services") was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor, alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation campuses from Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, at the center of the company's operations.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
The QTS Ashburn Lockridge campus holds 75 MW of planned IT capacity across a 24-acre, 2-building site in Sterling, Virginia, placing it as a secondary facility within Virginia's data center footprint rather than a regional constraint on AI power availability.

Virginia as a whole claims 1,375 MW across 23 disclosed facilities. The Ashburn Lockridge campus, at 75 MW, ranks below Virginia's top tier and accounts for roughly 5 percent of the state's published capacity. This positions it as incremental supply to an already-mapped region. QTS operates as part of Blackstone's portfolio following its August 2021 acquisition for approximately 10 billion dollars, giving the facility backing from a major institutional operator with existing scale across multiple states.

The campus sits within QTS's Northern Virginia footprint, which spans Loudoun and Prince William Counties alongside a separate Richmond facility. At conservative density estimates, the 75 MW capacity translates to approximately 1,875 racks, though actual deployment density remains unpublished. No information discloses tenant mix, grid interconnection status, power purchase agreements, or construction timeline. These gaps mean the data establishes capacity but not whether this site is currently constrained by power supply or grid access, or whether buildout timeline aligns with near-term AI demand.
